scoring.5: Closely reflects observed public user language, has one clear intent, and fits the platform surface.
scoring.4: Natural fixed editorial synthesis supported by observed themes, with minor construction or combined criteria.
scoring.3: Plausible but noticeably designed for research or weakly evidenced.
scoring.2: Formal, stacked, or unlike an ordinary request.
scoring.1: Implausible as a real user request.
scoring.slot_score_rule: The semantic slot score is the lowest score among its four platform renderings.

notes: ChatGPT, Gemini, and Copilot use conservative conversational variations; no unsupported platform dialect is invented.
Google AI Overview deliberately mixes concise searches and full questions because current official guidance says users ask both conventional and longer complex queries.
A platform rendering may change syntax but may not add or remove a decision criterion from its semantic slot.
